sources.title: Scaling up Test-Time Compute with Latent Reasoning: A Recurrent Depth Approach
inspected_locators: S3.SS1: recurrent state equation s_i=R(e,s_(i-1)) and coda on s_r
S3.SS3: objective expectation over sampled r and truncated backpropagation caveat
S5.SS1: matched-training baseline in Table 4 and explicit training/FLOP caveats
short_excerpts: Given an init random state ... the model repeatedly applies the core block R ... and outputs a new latent state ... After finishing all iterations, the coda block processes the last state.
We optimize the expectation of the loss function ... over ... random iteration counts r ...
To keep computation and memory low at train time, we backpropagate through only the last k iterations of the recurrent unit.
Table 4: Baseline comparison, recurrent versus non-recurrent model trained in the same training setup and data.
sources.scope: Supports variable-depth recurrence, sampled terminal-depth objective, chain-truncation caveat and matched-comparison practice. The paper does not establish odd-to-even generalization for this proposed {1,3,5} course recipe.

sources.title: Autograd mechanics
sources.version: The inspected HTML title says PyTorch 2.8 documentation; the canonical URL in those original bytes is stable.
short_excerpts: By tracing this graph from roots to leaves, you can automatically compute the gradients using the chain rule.
Non-leaf tensors ... have a backward graph associated with them. Thus their gradients will be needed as an intermediary result to compute the gradient for a leaf tensor that requires grad.
sources.scope: Supports the reverse chain-rule path through intermediate states when the graph is retained. It does not promise nonzero gradients or gradients through detach/no_grad. This is a mathematical mechanism source; the separately executed local example records its actual torch 2.14.1+cpu environment.
